2. On 25.11.89 Sufi Mia filed a petition of complaint against the accused-petitioners alleging that on 18-11-89 the accused petitioners forming an unlawful assembly and armed with deadly weapons went to cut away paddy from the land of Khalilur Rahman and, on being resisted, the accused-petitioners assaulted the men of the complainant including one Velon Mia causing injuries to them. The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence being CR case No.143 of 1989 against the accused-petitioners under sections 323, 324 and 325 of the Penal Code and issued warrants of arrest against them. On 31-12-89 the complainant (Sufi Mia) moved the court of the learned Magistrate with an application seeking permission to compound the offence stating that on the advice of and at the intervention of the village elders and well-wishers of the parties, the case had been settled. On the same day (31-12-89), the learned Magistrate allowed the application for composition of the offence and passed an order of acquittal of the accused persons under section 248 of the Criminal Procedure Code. On 16-1-90 Velon Mia, one of the victims of the first case (CR case No. 143 of 1989) filed a petition of complaint on the same occurrence and against the same set of accused-petitioners and the learned Magistrate took cognisance of the offence being CR case No. 14 of 1990 against the accused persons under sections 323, 324 and 326 of the Penal Code and issued warrants of arrest against them. The accused-petitioners have obtained the present Rule calling in question the accused prosecution in view of their acquittal in CR case No.143 of 1989 upon composition of the offence under section 345(6) of the CrPC (hereinafter referred to as the Code). 

 5. CR case No.143 of 1989 is under sections 323, 324 and 325 of the Penal Code, A perusal of section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shows that the persons to whom hurt is caused under section 323 may compound the offence under sub-section (1) thereof and similarly the person to whom the hurt is caused under section 324 or 325 of the Penal Code can compound an offence with the permission of the court under sub-section (2) of the said section. 

 6. On 31.12.89 the learned Magistrate, on perusal of the petition filed by the complainant, passed an order for compounding the offence in acquitting the accused persons under section 248 of the Code. In this connection we may quote the petition filed by complainant Sufi Mia in CR case No. 143 of 1989, which is as follows: 

 There is nothing to show either from the petition of compromise of Sufi Mia dated 31-12-89 or the order of the learned Magistrate of the same day that Velon Mia, one of the three victims of CR case No. 143 of 1989, was a party to the petition of compromise dated 31-12-89. An offence under section 323, 324 or 325 can be compounded by the person or persons to whom the hurt is caused. In the instant case the offence having not been compounded by Velon Mia, to whom hurt was caused the order of composition of the offence dated 31-12-89 suffers from legal infirmity and cannot operate as an acquittal of the accused persons so far as Velon Mia is concerned. In this view of the matter, Velon Mia is not debarred from prosecuting the accused for an offence, which has not been compounded by him. The doctrine of double jeopardy enunciated in section 403 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is hardly applicable to the facts of the present case. To take a different view is fraught with dangers as it may cause prejudice to the real victims, who may have suffered injuries.
